title: NY State Assembly · District 73
area: Manhattan's East Side, including the Upper East Side, Midtown East and parts of the Flatiron District.

context.text: Open seat: incumbent Alex Bores (D) is not seeking re-election to the Assembly; he ran for the U.S. House in New York's 12th Congressional District and lost in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary. Vanessa Aronson (D, WFP) is unopposed on the November ballot; she advanced from the Democratic and Working Families Party lines without a primary after her only would-be opponents withdrew — Nathaniel Gavronsky (Block Mamdani Party) withdrew, and Republican David Casavis withdrew before the canceled Republican primary.

candidates.name: Vanessa Aronson
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic and Working Families Party lines without opposition after other candidates withdrew; unopposed in the general election.

summary.text: Vanessa Aronson is the Democratic and Working Families Party nominee for the open NY State Assembly District 73 seat, running unopposed. She is a former public-school teacher and U.S. State Department foreign service officer who previously ran unsuccessfully for New York City Council District 4 in 2017 and 2025.

background.text: Earned a B.A. in political science from the University of Chicago, an M.A. in teaching from the Relay Graduate School of Education, and an M.P.P. in political advocacy and leadership from the Harvard Kennedy School.
Worked as a math and science teacher in New York City public schools.

Served as a U.S. Department of State foreign service officer, including as vice consul at the U.S. Consulate General in Ho Chi Minh City and as a food security officer in the department's Bureau of International Organization Affairs.
Ran unsuccessfully for New York City Council District 4 in 2017 and, in a ranked-choice Democratic primary, in 2025, losing to Virginia Maloney in the final round 53.1% to 46.9%.

priorities.text: Reducing the influence of lobbyists, particularly for business and real-estate interests, on government decisions.
Expanding oversight of police surveillance technology.
Continued legal representation for immigrants facing deportation proceedings.

positions.summary: In her 2017 city council candidate survey, said she would work to continue and fully fund New York's Immigrant Family Unity Project, which provides free legal counsel to low-income immigrants facing deportation.
positions.quote: As your City Council member, I will work to continue this program and ensure it is fully funded in the future so that no New Yorker facing deportation goes to immigration court without qualified representation.

candidates.researchNotes: Aronson has not held elected office, so there is no official voting or bill-sponsorship record. Her only completed Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey dates to her 2017 City Council run; no updated 2026 Assembly campaign website could be reached (vanessataronson.com did not resolve), so her documented priorities and the one mapped issue position reflect that earlier survey rather than confirmed current statements for this race.
